question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{9{x}^{3}-4x}{3{x}^{2}+2x} & =\frac{9(0)^{3}-4(0)}{3(0)^{2}+2(0)}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9{x}^{3}-4x}{3{x}^{2}+2x} & =\frac{x(9{x}^{2}-4)}{x(3x+2)} \\  & =\frac{9{x}^{2}-4}{3x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{9{x}^{3}-4x}{3{x}^{2}+2x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{9{x}^{2}-4}{3x+2} \\  & =\frac{0-4}{0+2} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
